extracted.intended_audience: PR and marketing professionals, content marketers, and SEO specialists creating press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for writing, structuring, and distributing press releases to maximize SEO value (both organic search and Google News), including on-site newsroom strategy, wire distribution timing, keyword placement, linking, schema, and multimedia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire releases generate nofollow backlinks
rubrics_metrics.description: Wire-distributed press releases typically create nofollow backlinks, providing limited direct SEO 'juice'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on wires alone for follow links; view wire links as limited for link equity. Use wires for distribution but combine with other tactics for real link value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earned media coverage provides real SEO value
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary SEO benefit comes from journalists and outlets picking up the release and providing followed backlinks (earned coverage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize outreach to journalists and tactics that generate earned mentions; evaluate success by whether coverage results in followed backlinks rather than just wire pulls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press releases function as keyword anchors for newsroom pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Hosting the press release on your company's newsroom helps build keyword-targeted pages that can rank for branded/topic queries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish a newsroom version first to establish SEO ownership and anchor keyword relevance; the newsroom page can be optimized and linked internally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize press releases for both Google and Google News
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases should be written and structured to perform in organic search and to be eligible/relevant for Google News.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Google News signals (multimedia, timeliness, clear metadata/schema) in addition to standard SEO copy best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary keyword in headline (front-loaded)
rubrics_metrics.description: Place the main target keyword in the headline and as early (front-loaded) as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Front-loading improves SERP relevance and clarity; avoid awkward phrasing but ensure the keyword appears near the start of the headline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the primary keyword in the first paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeat the primary keyword within the first paragraph of the body to reinforce topical relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural usage is key — include the keyword early but avoid forced or repetitive phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary keywords in subheaders (H2/H3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Place supporting/secondary keywords in H2 or H3 subheaders to improve scannability and keyword coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use subheaders to break content into topical sections and to incorporate secondary phrases without keyword-stuffing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand name + keyword combination once
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the combination of your brand name and the target keyword once in the copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using brand+keyword once helps branded search relevance but avoid overusing the combo which can look spammy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid keyword stuffing
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not unnaturally repeat keywords; Google penalizes keyword-stuffed content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write for humans first; ensure keyword placement is natural and adds value. Keyword density should not compromise readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline length: 60 characters or less
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep headlines at 60 characters or fewer so they display fully in SERPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shorter headlines reduce truncation risk. If you must be longer, ensure the most important words appear within the first 60 characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include brand name in headline only if it's a recognized search term
rubrics_metrics.description: Only add the brand to the headline when the brand itself is a meaningful search term for users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid appending the brand in every headline; include it when it adds search relevance or trust signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use numbers in headlines when relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Include numerals (e.g., '5 tips', '2026 results') when they improve clarity and CTR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbers can increase click-through but should be factual and relevant, not clickbait-y.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid clickbait headlines (wire services may reject them)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use sensational or misleading headlines — wire services can reject clickbait headlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft accurate, clear headlines that reflect the content; avoid hype that could trigger manual review or rejection by distribution services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimal body length: 400–700 words
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for a press release body length between 400 and 700 words for SEO and news value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This length balances sufficient detail for journalists and search relevance without being overly long; adapt as needed for the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use H2 subheaders for scannability
rubrics_metrics.description: Break the body into sections with H2 (and H3) subheaders to improve readability and SEO structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scannable structure helps human readers and search crawlers; use descriptive subheaders that can include secondary keywords.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include 1–2 outbound links to credible sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Add one to two external links pointing to authoritative, relevant sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outbound links to reputable sources add context and credibility; avoid over-linking externally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include 1–2 inbound links to your own pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Include one to two links back to relevant pages on your site (product, newsroom, supporting content).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link to the most relevant internal pages rather than repeatedly linking to the homepage; vary anchor text and destination appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use anchor text that matches target keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Use keyword-relevant anchor text for internal/external links when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer descriptive, relevant anchors over generic phrases; do not over-optimize anchor text to the point of sounding spammy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include alt text for any embedded images
rubrics_metrics.description: All images should have descriptive alt text to support accessibility and SEO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write concise, descriptive alt text that can include relevant keywords when appropriate, but avoid keyword stuffing in alt attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use NewsArticle schema if self-hosting
rubrics_metrics.description: When posting the release on your own site/newsroom, apply the NewsArticle structured data schema.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schema improves eligibility and appearance in Google News/serp features; implement accurately according to schema.org and Google guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include datePublished and dateModified in schema
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide publishing and modification timestamps in your structured data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate dates support timeliness signals for news indexing and trustworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add author and organization info in schema
rubrics_metrics.description: Include author and organization metadata in structured data to identify the source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent organization names and author attribution to improve credibility and potential rich result eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include headline and description in schema
rubrics_metrics.description: Populate headline and description fields in the schema markup for the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure schema headline/description match on-page content and are concise and accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include image schema for embedded media
rubrics_metrics.description: Add image-specific structured data for any embedded photos or media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Image schema can help Google understand and surface images in news contexts; include proper URLs, captions, and alt text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish newsroom version before wire distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Post the press release on your company newsroom first to establish the authoritative on-site version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing on your site first helps claim SEO ownership; ensure the newsroom page is optimized and contains schema and multimedia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay wire distribution 3–7 days after newsroom post for SEO ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Wait 3–7 days to distribute via wire so the newsroom version can be indexed and gain priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This delay can help the owned newsroom page rank instead of wire copies; balance timeliness needs with SEO strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct outreach to journalists for earned coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform targeted outreach to journalists to secure pickups that produce followed backlinks and coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personalized pitches and journalist relationships increase chances of earned coverage; measure success by actual coverage and link outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid linking repeatedly to the homepage
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not create multiple links pointing only to the homepage instead of relevant internal pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer contextual internal links to specific product or resource pages; too many homepage links dilute relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid generic anchor text (e.g., 'click here')
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic anchor text is unhelpful for users and SEO; prefer descriptive anchors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use anchor text that indicates the destination content and, where appropriate, includes relevant keywords naturally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not be wire-only without your own newsroom version
rubrics_metrics.description: Relying solely on wire distribution without a hosted newsroom version reduces your chance of capturing SEO benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always have an owned newsroom page to host the canonical version; wire-only approaches cede SEO ownership to wire services or republishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include multimedia (images) — Google News rewards images
rubrics_metrics.description: Add images and multimedia to increase Google News eligibility and engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality images with proper alt text and schema improve news signals; avoid low-quality or irrelevant media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement schema markup (do not omit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Missing structured data reduces the press release's chances for news-specific features and indexing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure schema is present and correct—omitting schema is a common SEO mistake that undermines Google News and rich-result potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric for SEO (summary checklist)
rubrics_metrics.description: A consolidated checklist: primary keyword front-loaded in headline; 60-character headline limit; 400–700 word body; subheaders for scannability; 1–2 inbound + 1–2 outbound links; schema markup if self-hosted; newsroom version + wire + earned outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this checklist as the core production standard: implement headline and body keyword placement, link strategy, schema, multimedia, and a distribution plan (own newsroom first, then wire, plus journalist outreach). Avoid the listed common mistakes.
